newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress sees new government in a week.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress sees new government in a week.

text.p: India's Congress party on Monday welcomed caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's offer to quit as head of the United Front coalition and said a new government could be formed in about one week.

"If they have any other leader, we are prepared to support them," Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told Reuters. Asked how long it would take the United Front and Congress to work out a new power-sharing deal, Gadgil said: "About a week."

Late on Sunday, Deve Gowda offered to step down as head of his 15-party coalition if it would lead to a new governing agreement with Congress, which provoked his downfall on Friday by withdrawing support for his 10-month-old government.
Gadgil said that provided the United Front replaced Deve Gowda, Congress was prepared to support the centre-left coalition from outside, meaning it would not take any ministerial portfolios.

The Congress spokesman said his party would not have any difficulty meeting a United Front demand that it withdraw a letter to President Shankar Dayal Sharma revoking its support for the United Front and staking a claim to power.

He said negotiations between the two political formations would continue, perhaps on Monday. The policy-making Congress Working Committee was set to meet on Monday at 7 p.m. (1330 GMT) to discuss the political situation.
